Strong agreement on PrE defects (C17-C18, C120-C121, C125, C131, C175-C176). Both accept the statistical significance and dose-dependent effects, treating this as a key finding on lineage segregation impairment.

Strong agreement on differential UPR response by dosage (C135-C137). Both accept the opposite enrichment patterns between high and low dosage groups as key mechanistic insight, treating this as part of the dose-dependent stress response.

Strong agreement on transcriptomic signatures and dose-dependent effects (C8-C9, C73-C75, C126). Both accept the RNA-seq data and GSEA analysis as convincing evidence for gene dosage-dependent transcriptomic responses.

Agreement on transcriptomic differences between natural and reversine-induced aneuploidy (C79-C80). Both accept this distinction as valid, supporting different cellular responses based on aneuploidy origin.

Partial overlap on dose-stratification analysis. Both accept dose-dependent transcriptomic responses (C83-C84, C133-C134) as key findings with clear PCA separation and progressive gene expression changes.

Minimal overlap on dose-dependent cell number effects (C122). Both accept this as part of the overall dose-response relationship demonstrating progressive impairment with increasing aneuploidy burden.
